candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — recognizing and explaining an appropriate palliative-care referral/consultation for a client with serious stroke
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize that palliative care after severe stroke can begin early and continue through recovery to address symptoms, values/goals communication, and patient-family support rather than being restricted to hospice or the final days of life.

options.A: Palliative care is generally reserved for the final days of life after disease-directed treatment has stopped.
options.B: Palliative care can be integrated now to address symptoms, communication about values and goals, and support for the client and family throughout recovery.
options.C: Palliative care is mainly used to determine hospice eligibility and should replace rehabilitation planning once consulted.
options.D: Palliative care should be delayed until the prognosis is certain so that recovery-focused care is not undermined.

candidate.rationale: The American Heart Association's 2024 scientific statement on palliative and end-of-life care in stroke emphasizes that palliative care should be integrated from the initial hospitalization and throughout stroke recovery, not limited to end-of-life. Core palliative-care skills include symptom management, effective communication, and understanding patient values and goals, while support extends to patients and families. Therefore, B is the best response. A and D incorrectly delay palliative care, and C incorrectly reduces palliative care to hospice and frames it as a replacement for rehabilitation rather than care that can be integrated across recovery.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Items 1, 2, and 9 directly support integrating palliative care from initial hospitalization through all phases of stroke recovery rather than limiting it to end-of-life; item 7 directly supports communication, symptom management, and attention to patient values and goals. The same AHA material identifies support for patients and families as part of the palliative approach.
candidate.source_document_title: Palliative and End-of-Life Care in Stroke: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
candidate.source_locator: American Heart Association Professional Heart Daily official supporting material, 'Top Things to Know: Palliative and End of Life Care in Stroke,' updated December 16, 2024, items 1, 2, 7, and 9; these summarize the linked Stroke scientific statement by Creutzfeldt et al., DOI 10.1161/STR.0000000000000479.
candidate.stem: A client with a severe stroke is receiving disease-directed treatment. The family asks why palliative care is being involved now. Which response by the nurse is most accurate?
